name: ryk-claude-mods
description: Claude Code mods (plugins built on TypeScript hook modules) for long sessions with many agents: context budgets and handoffs, compaction focus, standing goals, branch ownership, notification de-duplication, and memory and disk guards for macOS.

plugins.name: agent-budget
plugins.description: Tracks each agent's context size, warns as it grows and tells a subagent past the rotation threshold to write its handoff brief and stop.

plugins.name: branch-owners
plugins.description: Records which agent created each git branch and worktree, and lists the unmerged ones with their owners (/branch-owners).

plugins.name: focus-compact
plugins.description: Gives every compaction, automatic ones included, a standing focus; keeps each summary as a brief on disk; and escalates to a handoff when compaction stops paying (/focus-compact).

plugins.name: goal-refresh
plugins.description: Keeps a session's standing goal (and the native /goal condition) fresh in long sessions with a short reminder on turns already happening, and lets the goal be updated through discussion.

plugins.name: mem-watch
plugins.description: Watches macOS free memory and swap, shows them in the status line and alerts once when either crosses its limit. Until memory recovers, a light-list gate lets only reading, cleanup, file chores and everyday git run and refuses everything else (subagents, Docker, evals, builds). A cap holds each session to 4 top-level subagents and 3 background jobs at once, whatever memory says.

plugins.name: notice-dedupe
plugins.description: Drops task notifications that carry no information and near-exact repeats of notifications, failures, peer messages, scheduled prompts and agent messages, so they stop waking the main thread; counts what it drops across sessions.

plugins.name: storage-watch
plugins.description: Watches free disk space on the macOS data volume, shows it in the status line and alerts once as it falls through each tier (20, 10, 5, 1 GB). At or below 5 GB free, a light-list gate lets only reading, cleanup, file chores and everyday git run and refuses everything else (subagents, Docker, downloads, installs, tree copies). It has no concurrency cap; mem-watch holds that.
